title: Held-out observed-galaxy radial twin validation
purpose: Show separately whether a gravity formula predicts an observed rotation curve and whether the same prediction survives a formula-independent generated radial twin of the galaxy.
claimBoundaries: A radial twin is a compressed surrogate of published one-dimensional baryonic mass-model channels, not a photorealistic or uniquely reconstructed three-dimensional galaxy.
Agreement of generated-twin speeds with observations is joint evidence about source reconstruction and the tested gravity formula; the two errors must be reported separately.
SPARC has been repeatedly examined, so this is public spent validation rather than a blind holdout.
The held-out speed comparison tests circular-speed observations, not individual stellar trajectories or a resolved velocity field.
No success on radial twins establishes cluster lensing, Solar-System, cosmological, or relativistic validity.
